messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH severity — token_count anomaly for tenant=emerald-health (VPC: dedicated-pool-3). Metric: tokens_per_min jumped from ~120k to ~1.2M in 10m. Alert rule: tenant_tokens_rate > 3x baseline. Link: https://redwood.metrics/alerts/1791122334 :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: Got it, paging in. I'll take first touch. samir pinged for tokenization/encoding angle.

samir: I'm on. Quick triage: looking at request samples from the pool — the payloads appear to contain multibyte sequences and a mix of non-normalized apostrophes and a stray BOM in some requests. Running tokenizer locally shows token counts ~4-6x higher for these samples vs canonical ones.

maria: adding color from model side — we saw a client-side change last night where emerald-health switched their client lib to our new streaming uploader. That uploader does minimal normalization. If the customer is sending UTF-16/CRLF+surrogate pairs, our tokenizer can explode token counts.

support-jake: I just DM'd the Emerald account lead to ask whether they rolled any encoding/lib changes. They replied: "we upgraded to v2.1.0 of our SDK at 20:10 UTC, noticed higher costs but thought it was traffic."

samir: Copy. Repro steps I ran:
```
# reproduce tokenization diff
from redwood_tokenizer import encode
s1 = "They're looking — \u2018smart quotes\u2019 and \uFEFFBOM\uFEFF"
s2 = s1.encode('utf-16').decode('latin1')  # client could mistakenly send this
print(len(encode(s1)))  # expected 23 tokens
print(len(encode(s2)))  # observed 110 tokens
```
This matches the +x tokens behaviour.

elaine: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) isolate emerald-health to its own node pool (we already have them in dedicated-pool-3 but we should cordon traffic to a control node to stop cross-tenant noise). 2) apply a temporary pre-tokenizer normalization layer that forces UTF-8/NFC and strips BOM + replaces smart quotes. 3) pin them to a compatible model variant (open-compat-1.1) that has more conservative tokenization. 4) notify billing to hold auto-charges pending review.

oncall-sre: Executing 1 & 3 now. Cordon applied to dedicated-pool-3: `kubectl label node pool-3 emerald-quarantine=true` — routing will send emerald-health to quarantine-nodes. Pinning tenant to model=open-compat-1.1 via routing API.

deploy-bot: deploy started: ingress-normalizer@canary -> pods/ingress-normalizer-3bcd (image: rwinf/ingress-normalizer:sha-abc123).

samir: Good, while canary rolls I'll push a temp mitigation script that detects odd UTF-16 patterns and normalizes them before tokenization. Patch diff: `normalize_payloads` replaces BOMs and coerces to utf-8, NFC. Quick test on one live request now returns token count near baseline.

support-jake: Customer replied: "Thanks — we did upgrade SDK and saw higher token counts. We're pausing traffic while you do your checks." They've requested an interim summary and ETA.

elaine: Billing ops, please confirm hold. billing-ops: can you ack?

billing-ops: Acked. Put emerald-health on billing_hold=true and created ticket BILL-5872 to ensure no automated overage bill is issued while we investigate.

maria: Long-term fix proposals: 1) enforce canonical utf-8 ingestion on all ingress paths, 2) add a tokenization sanity-check alert per-tenant (tokens_per_request median > 3x expected), 3) add a documented SDK compatibility check (we should surface breaking changes). Also we should ship tokenizer-backed contract tests for SDK releases.

oncall-sre: Canary for ingress-normalizer is green on 2 pods. Prometheus shows token rate for emerald-health dropping back to ~140k/min. Rolling the normalizer to 100% for that tenant only.

incident-bot: Note: oncall change — samir handing off to elaine for post-incident follow-up. Handoff at 1791124034.

elaine: I'll take postmortem and customer comms. Action items I'll own: 1) postmortem doc, 2) RFC for ingress normalization, 3) add tenant-token-sanity alert, 4) coordinate billing credit with finance. Samir, can you add the tokenizer repro and unit test?

samir: Yep I'll open a PR with reproduction and unit tests.

support-jake: Drafted message to Emerald (sending now):
"Hi Emerald team — we identified an encoding mismatch triggered by your recent SDK upgrade that caused inflated token counts. We've applied a temporary normalization at our ingress and pinned your traffic to a compatible model. We've paused automated billing for the spike while we quantify impact. We'll follow up with a detailed report and recommended SDK patch. — Jake (Redwood Support)"

billing-ops: Finance notified; provisional credit approved up to $X pending final reconciliation. Ticket BILL-5872 updated.

maria: Recommendation for SDK teams: make encoding errors explicit in logs and provide a warning header when tokens_per_request deviates significantly after an SDK upgrade.

elaine: Closing out incident for now — ingress normalizer in prod for emerald-health, token rates back to expected, customer paused upgrade, billing hold in place. I'll publish the postmortem draft in #postmortems and loop in product & SDK owners.

incident-bot: Incident resolved? status=mitigated. Recording timeline and actions to Incident Tracker ID: INC-2026-emerald-enc-1791122334.

elaine: Follow-ups (quick list): 1) long-term ingress normalization RFC (2w), 2) SDK breaking-change checklist, 3) tenant-token alert + runbook, 4) billing reconciliation. Assigning owners in the doc.

support-jake: Emerald replied: "Thanks for the quick response. We'll patch to UTF-8 and rerun tests. Appreciate the credit hold." :heart:

incident-bot: Thread closed.
